summary: The bill amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Fair Housing Act to bar any lawsuits alleging unlawful employment or housing practices based on disparate impact, and nullifies related federal regulations that allow such claims.

Section 3 explicitly eliminates disparate-impact claims under Title VII for employment practices. This removes a legal tool workers and unions have used to challenge facially neutral employer policies that produce disproportionate effects, thereby tilting the balance toward employer flexibility.
The bill narrows anti-discrimination enforcement by barring disparate-impact claims but does not create or expand religious exemptions; any connection is indirect at best.
